thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: elevated SSE disconnect rate for /v1/stream (prod). Threshold breached: 8% -> 18% over 5m. Pager duty: maria.

maria (oncall): saw the page. investigating. can someone confirm customer impact scope?

rita (support): Support report from Kevin: intermittent partial responses when tool-call meta headers are present. He says clients see `payload truncated` at client side ~5-10s after open.

kevin (customer): Hi — we saw many streaming sessions drop mid-toolcall yesterday evening. We tried reconnect but state lost. A few users saw tool-call parsing errors in logs.

ashok (sre): grabbing infra metrics now. Early look: connection resets from frontend proxies to runtime workers increased. TCP FINs from worker side around same time as SSE disconnect spikes.

maria (oncall): mitigation? Can we route traffic to fallback region or reduce keepalive aggressiveness?\
ashok (sre): We can flip routing to dedicated pool with conservative TCP timeouts. I'll prepare a traffic-shift plan (20% -> 50% -> 100%) with guards.

dina (eng-runtime): hypothesis: a recent kernel patch + our new KV cache eviction pattern produces transient backpressure during function-call parsing which stalls EventStream flush. That could cause proxy to close connection.

owen (eng-ml): also seeing a bump in average tokens per request for tool-calls — more metadata being attached by some clients. May amplify memory pressure.

maria (oncall): runbook step: gather sample logs for dropped connections + extract last 100 bytes of stream before disconnect. ashok, can you capture?

ashok (sre): capturing now. grep for 502/stream-disconnect and `fncall` in runtime logs. saving to /tmp/stream-disconnect-snippets.log. snippet: ```
[2026-11-02T18:05:23Z] worker-12 INFO sse: write failed: write tcp 10.2.8.12:443->10.4.1.22:51234: write: connection reset by peer
[2026-11-02T18:05:23Z] worker-12 DEBUG fncall: parser error: unexpected token '\u0000' at pos 482
```

maria (oncall): good. include proxy (lb) logs too — need to know who initiated FIN.

ashok (sre): LB logs show FIN from runtime IPs; upstream closing. that aligns with runtime process failing writes.

dina (eng-runtime): can you paste full fncall parser trace from worker-12?

ashok (sre): pasted: ```
2026-11-02T18:05:22.997Z worker-12 ERROR fncall.parser: unexpected \u0000 in header at 0x1e2; raw: "...function":{...},"meta":"\u0000"
stack:
  at parseToolCall (/srv/runtime/fnparser.js:148)
  at handleStream (/srv/runtime/sse.js:402)
  at flushChunk (/srv/runtime/sse.js:450)
  at writeChunk (/srv/runtime/net.js:210)
```

owen (eng-ml): that NUL looks like client-side serialization bug or an encoding mismatch in the header metadata. Which client versions were connecting?

rita (support): Kevin's team uses SDK v1.8.3. We have records of other customers on older SDKs too.

kevin (customer): we rolled a small change to include binary metadata in headers. We tested locally; maybe some proxy stops sanitized NULs.

dina (eng-runtime): runtime shouldn't receive NUL in JSON headers — must escape. If it gets through, our parser chokes and raises exception which triggers worker to stop streaming and close connection. That's consistent.

maria (oncall): immediate mitigations: (1) implement tolerant parser that treats NUL as escaped and drops it, (2) route affected tenants to fallback non-streaming endpoint, (3) advise customer to revert SDK change. Which is fastest?

dina (eng-runtime): fastest short-term is a tolerant parser can be shipped as a hotfix in the routing layer — not full runtime rebuild. I can push a hairpin patch to sse-proxy within 10-15m to sanitize incoming headers.

ashok (sre): while we do that, I'll start a targeted traffic shift to dedicated pool for affected tenants. Can you list affected customer ids?

rita (support): affected: kevin-company (tenant id kc-77), and a couple of others on SDK v1.8.x — I'll DM full list to ashok.

evan (product): customer impact: how many users affected? ETA for fix? Do we need to page CS/AM?

rita (support): initial estimate: kc-77 had ~1200 active streaming sessions at peak; ~30% experienced disconnects. other tenants single-digit percent.

maria (oncall): timeline note for RCA: record when SDK change was deployed (kevin says 18:00 UTC), when disconnect spike started (18:05 UTC), when runtime exceptions appeared (18:05:22 UTC).

dina (eng-runtime): preparing small sanitizer patch now. core idea: run header values through `replace(/\u0000/g, '')` prior to JSON parse. will instrument to log sanitized occurrences.

ashok (sre): traffic-shift plan in progress: shifting kc-77 to dedicated pool at 18:20 -> 80% by 18:25. will monitor error rate + latency.

kevin (customer): we can rollback our SDK change if that helps. trying to push a revert now.

dina (eng-runtime): hotfix pushed to sse-proxy canary at 18:18. logs: ```
[18:18:05] proxy-2 INFO sse-sanitize: found_nul=43 tenant=kc-77 session=abc123
[18:18:05] proxy-2 INFO sse-sanitize: sanitized_headers
```

maria (oncall): ashok — post-hotfix metrics?

ashok (sre): error rate dropped from 18% -> 4% within 2m of canary. shifting kc-77 complete at 18:26. residual disconnects now mostly client-initiated retries.

owen (eng-ml): good sign. we still need long-term fix: runtime parser should be hardened and tests added for binary metadata in headers and cross-proxy encodings.

dina (eng-runtime): agreed. follow-ups: (A) add parser fuzz tests and NUL-tolerant code path, (B) add explicit validation and 400-level reject earlier so worker doesn't crash, (C) add metric alert for sanitized header rate.

maria (oncall): action items captured. I'll handoff to engineering for RCA write-up. oncall -> ashok + dina at 18:35.

ashok (sre): handing over. continuing to monitor. setting incident state to "mitigated".

evan (product): customer comms: Rita, can you confirm customer-facing summary and recommend SDK rollback or upgrade with escaping?

rita (support): will draft: "We deployed a hotfix to sanitize unexpected binary NUL characters in streaming headers. We recommend rolling back the SDK change while we add formal support to the runtime and validate. Apologies for the disruption — CS will follow up with impacted customers."

kevin (customer): thanks — we'll revert and coordinate test window. appreciate the quick fix.

maria (oncall): final notes for in-incident RCA thread: log bundle: /artifacts/incidents/1809123456-logs.tar.gz, canary patch id: c9f7a, affected tenants list (DMed), root cause hypothesis: client-side binary metadata produced NUL chars which bypassed upstream sanitization and crashed runtime parser; proximate cause: parser crash triggered worker-side FINs.

dina (eng-runtime): I'll own the postmortem and include timeline, sanitized counts, and code changes. planning a follow-up PR with tests and a safer reject path.

ashok (sre): leaving monitoring alerts on for 24h. setting a regression watch.

incident-bot: Incident state updated to MITIGATED by maria at 1809123876

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. closing handoff. if regressions occur, reopen thread or page oncall. :thumbsup:
